scope: Bounded Rust prototype for application-admitted work plus controlled real SDK calls. Windows host, synthetic loopback HTTP and memory stores; no production/disposable homeserver instances started.

source_inventory.contract: Clone over Arc<ClientInner>; no public global stop-and-join API.
Spawned response processor joined on normal return; cancellation of outer call can detach it.
Wrapper aborts on drop and joins on HTTP success; abort is not a completion acknowledgement.
Caller awaits response processing, handlers and outgoing requests on normal return.
Handler futures awaited inline; dropping registration does not join an active callback.
Takes one setup_e2ee handle; cancelling waiter can detach it; errors logged, unit returned.
Listener initialized on client construction; Drop aborts without join; no public complete stop API.
AfterDecryptionFailure only, not default Manual; listener abort does not recursively join child tasks.
Separate observer after recovery setup; not joined by setup waiter.
Startup/listener tasks; release build has no public join; history-on-invite enabled by builder default.
Background subscriber work opt-in; existing Matrix fixtures do not subscribe.
Globally enabled, per-room worker lazy; disabling does not join in-flight sends; fixtures send directly.
Disables queues/closes stores; requires prior sync stop; not an encryption task drain.
Concurrent requests log individual failures; wrapper success alone is not proof of key delivery.
Monitored handles expose abort and status; no recursive joined shutdown of SDK task groups.
Timeout/background shutdown may leak blocking work; not a completion acknowledgement.

source_inventory.anchor_pattern: Awaiting a `&mut JoinHandle<T>` is cancel safe
source_inventory.contract: Borrowed JoinHandle wait is cancellation-safe; dropping the owned JoinHandle detaches its task.

implementation.sdk_completion_proof: No proof issued: TrackedDrain.require_full_sdk_drain always rejects.

real_sdk_observations.init_http_response: Controlled HTTP503 released via Notify; joining initialization is not proof of healthy initialization.

failures_and_rechecks.cause: A mechanical edit added the stop handle without updating the two SDK loops. Fixed loops to consult signal only after full SDK calls; final check passed.

limits: No public SDK API joins all backup, recovery, historic bundle, cache and queue tasks. Task inventory is for the pinned minimal profile; new features need renewed inventory.
This prototype tracks only tasks and callback leases registered with it. Drop closes admission but detached work may continue; it never certifies completion.
Client::pause uses memory stores in the negative control. No persistent store handoff, filesystem lock release, remote logout/revocation, runtime/process isolation or memory/key erasure proof.

Plain synthetic timeline callbacks exercise actual classic/native SDK processing; this turn did not rerun real-homeserver SAS/Megolm messaging or encrypted restart scenarios. Native E2EE extensions are enabled, but no claim of exhaustive outgoing crypto failure/child-task coverage.
SDK initialization waiter returns unit and logs errors; wrapper completion alone cannot establish encryption health. send_outgoing_requests also logs individual failures.
Only Windows tests executed; no native Linux/macOS desktop or packaged controls tested.
required_next_contract: Close admission and unregister future producers for every activated SDK task group.
Expose retained completion handles for initialization, response processing, backup listeners and children, recovery, bundles and activated cache/queue tasks.
Keep pending shutdown ownership after deadline or caller cancellation; no completion token on timeout, task failure or unknown work.
Cooperatively finish non-cancellable response/store processing before closing any store or starting a new owner.
Propagate initialization and task outcomes and keep remote logout result separate from local shutdown.
Test real encrypted stores, delayed backup children, queued sends, callbacks, repeated lock/unlock, logout then different account, and all supported desktop platforms.
